culturalBackground: Children's mehndi uses small, simple motifs that can be finished in a few minutes.
Children's skin is more sensitive than adults', so only natural henna paste should be used.
Black henna often contains PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause serious skin reactions, and should never be used on children.
Henna should not be used on babies, and children with G6PD deficiency should avoid it; ask a doctor if you are unsure.
applicationTips: Pick a design that takes five to ten minutes; young children rarely sit still for longer.
Leave the paste on for a shorter time, around one to two hours, and wash hands well afterwards.
Do a patch test on the inner arm a day before, especially the first time a child wears mehndi.

faqPool.a: Natural henna is generally safe for older children, but do a patch test first. Avoid it for babies and for children with G6PD deficiency, and never use black henna.
Small flowers, hearts, stars and butterflies on the back of the hand are quick to apply and easy for children to enjoy.

faqPool.q: How do I keep a child from smudging mehndi?
faqPool.a: Choose a small design on the back of the hand and keep the child busy with a story or video until the paste dries.
